## Overall Assessment The student has made significant progress towards completing the refactoring exercise, but there are still several areas that need improvement.

Refactoring Steps Implementation:

- User.java - Fully implemented
- PostgresDriver.java - Partially implemented (missing constructor and getters/setters)
- RegularUserService.java - Not implemented (uses direct instantiation of PostgresDriver, violating DIP)
- AdminUserService.java - Not implemented (extends RegularUserService but does not override deleteAccount method)
- UserOperations.java - Partially implemented (interface is missing some required methods and has incorrect names for the methods provided)

## SOLID Violations

- SRP: User.java - User - Class has 9 methods, suggesting too many responsibilities
- Package Structure: Project Structure - Missing required package: solid.persistence.drivers
- Package Structure: PostgresDriver in solid.persistence - Implementation PostgresDriver should be in package solid.persistence.drivers, but found in solid.persistence
- DIP violation (UserService depends on concrete implementation of PostgresDriver): UserService constructor accepts DatabaseDriver, but RegularUserService and AdminUserService use direct instantiation of PostgresDriver.
- LSP violation (AdminUserService changes expected behavior of deleteAccount method): DeleteAccount in AdminUserService does not call super.DeleteAccount, which could cause unexpected behavior if the superclass implementation is changed or removed.
6. OCP violation (UserOperations interface has too many methods and is missing required methods for correct implementation): UserOperations interface has 13 methods, but only 4 are actually implemented in RegularUserService and AdminUserService. The remaining methods should be added to the interface.

## Improvement Suggestions

- Add constructor with DatabaseDriver parameter to PostgresDriver.java
- Create getters/setters for all fields in PostgresDriver.java
- Remove direct instantiation of PostgresDriver from RegularUserService and AdminUserService, replacing it with a constructor that accepts a DatabaseDriver (following DIP)
- Add override for deleteAccount method in AdminUserService to call super.deleteAccount() (following LSP)
- Add required methods to UserOperations interface based on the implementations found in RegularUserService and AdminUserService (following OCP).
6. Review overall class design and structure, focusing on separating responsibilities among classes and interfaces.

## Overall Assessment The student has completed most of the 5 refactoring steps and partially implemented one, but there are some issues with DIP violations.

Refactoring Steps Implementation:

- User class is split into three separate classes - Fully implemented
- NotificationService is refactored to use a dependency injection framework - Partially implemented (missing constructor injection for DatabaseDriver)
- UserService is refactored to use a dependency injection framework - Partially implemented (missing constructor injection for DatabaseDriver)
- PostgresDriver is moved into its own subpackage - Fully implemented
- Direct instantiation of PostgresDriver is removed - Partially implemented (constructor injection missing)

## SOLID Violations

- LSP violation in AdminUser.deleteAccount - Please check that deleting an admin user does not change the expected behavior.
- DIP violation in UserService - Please ensure that the constructor for UserService accepts a DatabaseDriver and is used to inject the dependency into the class.
- DIP violation in PostgresDriver - Please move PostgresDriver into its own subpackage.
- DIP violation in PostgresDriver instantiation - Please remove direct instantiation of PostgresDriver from UserService.

## Improvement Suggestions

- For LSP violations, please ensure that deleting an admin user does not change the expected behavior. If it does, consider adding a new abstract method to the base class and overriding it in the AdminUser subclass.
- For DIP violations, please ensure that the constructor for UserService accepts a DatabaseDriver and is used to inject the dependency into the class. This will allow for easier testing and maintenance of the code.
- For DIP violations, please move PostgresDriver into its own subpackage. This will help maintain a clear hierarchy of classes in the package and make it easier to manage dependencies between them.
- For DIP violations, please remove direct instantiation of PostgresDriver from UserService. This will allow for easier testing and maintenance of the code, as well as reducing coupling between classes. Instead, use dependency injection to inject an instance of PostgresDriver into the class.
